brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Off-cycle edition. It covers the 24 hours to 15:24 CEST on 17 October; new research covers 05:35 to 15:24 CEST, and items from earlier editions still inside the 24 hours were re-checked and carried.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Russia hits energy sites in ten regions in what Zelensky calls one of the largest grid strikes yet; seven killed, and Zaporizhstal is hit for a fifth time

sections.text: Kharkiv regional head Oleh Syniehubov said Russian strikes on the Slobidskyi and Nemyshlianskyi districts left 10 people affected, among them two 13-year-olds [1]. Mayor Ihor Terekhov said Banderol munitions hit Nemyshlianskyi several times, damaging residential buildings and breaking more than 100 windows [2]. Early on 17 October the Air Force warned of ballistic missiles toward Kryvyi Rih, Zaporizhzhia, Kamianske, and Dnipro, and Kyiv declared a red-level missile alert [3]. Zaporizhzhia's Ivan Fedorov reported several missile strikes on the city, damaged buildings and two people injured, according to preliminary information [4]. In a later update Fedorov said three residential buildings were damaged and cars had caught fire [5]. Suspilne correspondents reported explosions in Zaporizhzhia and repeated explosions in Kryvyi Rih; citing Kherson's city military administration, Suspilne reported that a Russian airstrike on Kherson injured an 11-year-old girl, that a paramedic was wounded in a repeat strike, that two more men were hospitalised after the overnight airstrike on the Korabelnyi district, and that a family with a one-month-old baby was injured in their flat by a morning airstrike [6]. The Dnipropetrovsk regional administration said Russian forces struck an industrial enterprise in Kryvyi Rih and that it was still establishing whether anyone was hurt [7]. Ukrenergo said restrictions for industry and business apply in all regions on 17 October, with hourly household outages in some regions, after Russian attacks on the grid [8]. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 332 attack drones and decoys, four sea-launched Kalibr cruise missiles, Kh-22/32 cruise missiles, and Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles overnight; 289 drones and the four Kalibrs were downed or jammed, and hits were recorded at 22 locations [9]. The Energy Ministry said energy facilities in ten regions, including Vinnytsia, Volyn, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Ternopil, Khmelnytskyi, and Kharkiv, were hit; power had been restored to more than half a million consumers, and hourly outage schedules were in force even in western regions [10]. RBC-Ukraine noted that on 16 October Putin ordered the strikes to continue after Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov reported that massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities had begun [10]. Zelensky called it one of the largest strikes on the energy system, with more than 15 key generation and transmission facilities targeted, and regional authorities put the toll over the past day at seven killed and about 90 injured [11]. Al Jazeera, citing Ukrainian officials, reported that Friday's attacks killed at least eight people in nine regions and that more than a million people lost power [12]. Metinvest said six ballistic missiles hit Zaporizhstal's internal energy and logistics infrastructure and blast-furnace areas at dawn, the plant's fifth such attack and 23 ballistic missiles in all, with no casualties this time [13]. Sloviansk city council said FAB-250 bombs hit two high-rise buildings at 03:40, killing one person and injuring ten [14].

Confidence on the scale of the attack and the energy damage is moderate, because the Air Force, the Energy Ministry, the President, and regional officials agree, but no independent or Russian account of the targets was found. Confidence on the Zaporizhstal strike is moderate, because it rests on the operator's statement carried by one agency.

items.title: Trump waives most Graham Act sanctions; Zelensky calls the diesel deal 'the first step' toward more relief as Moscow hails a 'historic moment'

sections.text: The White House posted an executive order in which Trump said he was waiving the sanctions, restrictions, and duties of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and had certified to Congress that the waiver is in the US national interest; the same order formally sets a 500 percent duty on Russian goods and a 100 percent duty on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, both subject to the waiver [15]. Reuters reported that the order came days before the measures were to take effect and noted that India, among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, had raised concerns about the law [16]. AP called the move unexpected and placed it a week after Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel [17]. CBS News reported that the 100 percent tariffs had been due on Sunday and that the waivers stay in place until officials determine further action is appropriate [18]. DW reported that the White House gave no explanation of how the pause serves the national interest [19]. The Wall Street Journal described it as a halt to most of the sanctions in the bill and part of a pivot toward Moscow [20]. Democratic Representative Don Beyer said Trump had waived all of the law's Russia sanctions and called on Congress to fix it [21]. On 16 October House Foreign Affairs ranking member Gregory Meeks introduced a bipartisan bill to void the Treasury licences behind the diesel deal and mandate sanctions on Russian energy [22]. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the waiver an important and truly historic moment and said the sanctions would have damaged mainly the US economy and global markets [23][24]. On Saturday Zelensky told reporters that the decision to scrap the law was wrong, that the diesel deal was only the first step and more sanctions relief would follow, that Putin feels joy at such support, and that energy strikes cannot be stopped by restricting Ukraine's response [25][26]. He said Kyiv had no warning of the waiver or the diesel deal and learned of a possible energy truce from the media [27].

Confidence on the waiver itself is high, because the primary text and five independent sources agree. Confidence on the reactions is high, because both sides' statements are on record and quoted consistently by independent outlets.

items.title: Ukrainian drones close Moscow's airports for a sixth night; Russia's Defence Ministry claims 610 drones downed as Ryazan's main crude unit is reported halted

sections.text: Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defences downed 25 more drones heading for the capital, bringing the night's total to 69, with emergency crews at debris sites and no reported casualties; Vnukovo, Domodedovo, Sheremetyevo, and Zhukovsky were not receiving or dispatching flights, according to Rosaviatsiya [28]. Moscow city media reported Sheremetyevo restrictions at about 02:03 Moscow time, putting all four airports under limits [29]. Interfax logged closures at Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky from 22:38 CEST, nine drones downed over Tula region, restrictions at Sochi, and later closures at Kostroma, Yaroslavl, Penza, Saratov, Gelendzhik, and Cherepovets; earlier the Russian Defence Ministry said 47 Ukrainian drones had been destroyed since Friday morning [30]. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the domestic petrol market still has a deficit of about 5 percent and that oil companies have postponed refinery maintenance [31]. The Kyiv Independent reported this was the sixth consecutive night of flight restrictions over Moscow since Kyiv resumed refinery strikes [32]. Russia's Defence Ministry later said air defences destroyed 610 Ukrainian drones between 20:00 on 16 October and 08:00 on 17 October Moscow time over 15 regions, Crimea, the Moscow region, and the Black Sea [33]. The Kyiv Independent, citing a Reuters report based on unnamed industry sources, said the Ryazan refinery halted its CDU-6 crude distillation unit after a drone attack on 15 October, and noted that Kyiv had reported no new refinery attacks since lifting its strike pause [34].

Confidence on the airport closures is high, because Russian officials and independent flight-tracking agree. Confidence on the drone counts is low, because only the defending side has given figures. Confidence on the Ryazan unit is low, because it rests on unnamed industry sources, single-source, unconfirmed.

items.title: Moscow repeats its Dobropillia claim and lists eight settlements in a day; Kyiv still reports fighting there, and ISW calls the claims exaggerated

sections.text: Defence Minister Andrei Belousov sent congratulations to brigades the ministry said had taken Dobropillia, Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, and Serhiivka in Donetsk region and Velykomykhailivka in Dnipropetrovsk region [35]. Ukraine's General Staff said in its 22:00 Kyiv-time update that 208 engagements took place, that 26 Russian assaults were repelled on the Pokrovsk axis including near Dobropillia and Serhiivka, and that fighting continued near Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka on the Kostiantynivka axis [36]. ISW assessed that Putin and Gerasimov are presenting greatly exaggerated advance figures, that its evidence shows Russia has taken about 100 square kilometres since 1 January, and that Russia has had a net loss of 122 square kilometres since 1 September [37]. Telegraf, citing DeepState map data as of 16 October, put the nearest Russian positions about 3.4 km from Dobropillia, about 4 km from Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, and about 4.9 km from Serhiivka, and cited the Conflict Intelligence Team as saying Russian troops are present on the southern outskirts of Dobropillia and east of it, without a firm view on how stable that presence is [38]. Reuters reported that Ukraine made no mention of Dobropillia changing hands [39]. On Saturday the Defence Ministry's daily report repeated the claims and added Pervomaiske in Donetsk region, Palamarivka and Kovalivka in Kharkiv region, and Malokaterynivka in Zaporizhzhia region, eight settlements in all [40]. No Ukrainian confirmation of any of the eight was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the two parties directly contradict each other and the open-source checks from DeepState, CIT, and ISW agree with each other but lag events by a day or more.

items.title: Telegraph says Musk proposed the Starlink speed cap to Trump; Trump says it was neither of them

sections.text: The Kyiv Independent, citing The Telegraph and four sources familiar with the matter, reported that Elon Musk approached Trump with the idea of restricting Starlink speeds for Ukrainian forces and that Trump agreed; the Telegraph said two Ukrainian sources and a senior European official confirmed the account [41]. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said it was not him and he did not think it was Musk, that he was not sure the service had been slowed at all, and that his relationship with Zelensky is good [42]. The BBC reported Trump's denial alongside Musk's earlier statement that Starshield limits are decided by the US military and ultimately the president, and Reuters' earlier report that the order came from inside the White House [43]. Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Washington, Denys Senik, told Newsmax2 that service was better than two days earlier but speeds still fluctuated, and that Kyiv was waiting for the Pentagon and SpaceX to clarify whether it had been fully restored [44].

Confidence on Trump's denial is high, because two independent sources carry his on-record words. Confidence on who ordered the cap is low, because the three accounts conflict and all rest on interested or anonymous sources.

items.title: Putin says Russia's 'security zone' inside Ukraine is not up for negotiation and claims about 6,500 sq km taken this year

sections.text: Reuters reported that Putin, in uniform at a command post, said Russia is establishing a "security zone" inside Ukraine along the border and does "not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations"; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the planned zone spans 660 km, of which 70% is under Russian control, without giving its depth [45]. RIA Novosti carried Putin's words at an auxiliary command post of the joint group of forces [46]. Kommersant reported the claims made at the command-post meeting that Russian forces had taken about 6,500 sq km and 310 settlements this year [47]. At 18:33 CEST Zelensky wrote that Putin "wants to destroy us" and asked whether the eastern part of the country would be enough for him [48]. Separately, the BBC reported from a Ukrainian counter-offensive, Operation Vivaldi, which Kyiv says has retaken 277 sq km in Donbas in recent months [49].

Confidence on Moscow's negotiating position is high, because Putin said it on camera and Reuters and Russian outlets agree on the wording. Confidence on the territorial figures is low, because only the Russian General Staff has given them.

items.title: Putin and Pope Leo XIV discuss Oleshky by phone; the Vatican seeks a ceasefire for aid and evacuation

sections.text: Vatican News said Pope Leo XIV spoke with Putin, raised concern over the situation in occupied Oleshky, and called for a ceasefire to allow humanitarian aid and the voluntary, safe evacuation of civilians [50]. The Kremlin readout, published at 17:35 CEST, blamed "the Kyiv regime" for the humanitarian situation there, said Putin supported the Vatican's intention to help the population and supplies, and said the two agreed to work together on this [51].

Confidence that the call took place and on its stated topics is high, because both parties published readouts. Confidence on any practical arrangement is low, because no operational detail has been published.

items.title: UN monitors say September civilian casualties in Ukraine were 85% higher than a year earlier

sections.text: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine said it verified at least 328 civilians killed and 2,105 injured in September, 85 per cent more than in September 2025, across 22 regions and Kyiv, with casualties on 22 of the month's 30 days. Mission head Danielle Bell said: "The first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years." The update cited 22 civilians killed in Pryluky on the night of 6 to 7 October [52]. AP carried the same report alongside the overnight strikes [53].
Confidence is high, because the figures come from the UN monitoring mission's own release and a wire carried them unchanged.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Moldova condemns Russia after five drones it identifies as Russian crash on its territory in under 24 hours

sections.text: Moldova's foreign ministry condemned repeated violations of its airspace on 15-16 October as a serious violation of sovereignty and territorial integrity and called on Russia to stop attacking Ukraine; the ministry said six unauthorised drone overflights were recorded on 15-16 October, one of which crashed and exploded in Donduseni district [1][2]. Reuters reported that five drones identified by Moldovan authorities as Russian entered over a little more than 17 hours on Thursday and Friday and all crashed, mainly in northern and eastern districts, lightly injuring one person and causing minor damage [3]. Reuters noted the ministry has repeatedly summoned Russian ambassador Oleg Ozerov over such incidents [3]. DW reported that the defence ministry said the Donduseni drone entered Moldovan airspace at 16:22 local time on 16 October and was declared crashed and exploded at 17:06, and counted it as the eighth violation of Moldovan airspace since 10 October [4]. Moldova's Defence Ministry put the week's total at seven airspace incidents between 10 and 16 October, including fragments of a drone with explosives found in Anenii Noi district on 10 October, and 63 incidents so far this year [5]. DW's Ukrainian service carried the condemnation and the tally on Saturday morning [6].
Confidence is moderate, because the facts of the crashes rest on the Moldovan government, repeated by one wire and one public broadcaster, and the type identification is not independently confirmed.

items.title: Romania keeps searching for seven Wine Trader sailors as a NATO military source says the drones came from Russia; Moscow repeats there is no evidence

sections.text: Reuters reported that Romania resumed the search on Friday for seven sailors missing from the San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader, with a Black Hawk placing four rescuers aboard, and that a NATO military source said the drones that hit it and the Yara J came from Russia [7]. Reuters counted at least five other cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in the past 10 days, with 23 sailors dead or missing, most outside NATO territorial waters [7]. In a Euronews interview President Nicusor Dan called for greater NATO oversight of the Black Sea and said it would only become safe after the war ends [8]. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, quoted by TASS, said there is no evidence of any party's involvement in the attacks in Bulgaria's economic zone; Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told parliament Russia was probably behind them but this cannot be proven [9].

Confidence on the search and the casualty tally is moderate, because one wire and Romanian officials agree. Confidence on Russian origin is low, because it rests on one anonymous source, single-source, unconfirmed.

items.title: Bulgaria formally asks NATO for combat aircraft, air defence, and anti-drone systems after the Black Sea ship strikes

sections.text: Reuters reported Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov saying Bulgaria had sent letters to the NATO Secretary General and the Supreme Allied Commander asking for additional forces on its territory and was awaiting a decision; a NATO official said ambassadors would discuss the request further. Rutte met Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev and Romanian President Dan on Thursday and said NATO would adjust its deterrence and defence posture in the Black Sea as needed [10]. Bulgarian National Radio, citing BTA, quoted Stoyanov: "We have requested aircraft, surface-to-air missile systems, anti-drone systems, and patrol aircraft"; he said no specific assistance was yet confirmed and that Romania and the Baltic states had similar needs [11]. Defense News carried the Reuters report and Stoyanov's plan to meet his Romanian and Turkish counterparts [12]. No NATO decision on the request had been published by the cutoff.
Confidence on the request is high, because the defence minister's on-record statement is carried consistently by a wire, the national radio, and a defence outlet.

items.title: Romania co-hosts NATO's annual hybrid-threats symposium and drafts a national counter-drone action plan with US support

sections.text: Romania's foreign ministry co-hosted NATO's annual symposium on hybrid threats on 15 and 16 October, where allied, EU, Moldovan, Ukrainian, and energy-industry participants discussed drone incidents, sabotage, cyber-attacks, disinformation, and threats to critical infrastructure, against what the ministry described as intensified actions attributed to Russia against Romania and the eastern flank [13]. US Ambassador Darryl Nirenberg said a four-day workshop at the Romanian Parliament ending on 16 October had produced a National Action Plan to detect, track, and neutralise aerial, surface, and underwater drones, covering the legal framework, inter-agency operations, and the protection of critical infrastructure [14].
Confidence is moderate, because each account rests on one outlet relaying an official source and the action plan itself was not published.

items.title: Finland sets a temporary restricted air and sea area over the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution against possible drones

sections.text: The Finnish Defence Forces said they had put a temporary restricted area in place over the eastern Gulf of Finland, for air and sea, from 03:36 Finnish time (02:36 CEST) [15]. A follow-up post said it was a precaution to protect bystanders and to give authorities the conditions to counter possible drones [15].
Confidence is moderate, because the source is the responsible authority itself but no other source confirmed the duration or trigger.

items.title: RAF crews logged two near misses with unidentified drones above 10,000 ft over the North Sea in February; police and external investigations are open

sections.text: Citing incident logs obtained by The Telegraph, GB News reported that an RAF Voyager tanker refuelling a Typhoon off Cromer on 18 February and a Typhoon in simulated combat five days later had close encounters with unidentified objects, one at 17,000 ft, neither visible on radar [16]. The Independent reported that the sightings near Norfolk and Humberside were passed to police, that multiple external investigations are ongoing, and that it was unclear whether the drones were hostile [17]. A Ministry of Defence spokesperson did not comment on the incidents directly but said enhanced vigilance had improved its ability to identify potential drone activity [17].

Confidence that the encounters were logged is moderate, because two outlets cite the same logs and the MoD did not dispute them. Confidence on the nature or origin of the objects is low, because no investigation finding exists.

items.title: Polish Starlink-station arson: German reporting ties the two Turkish suspects held in Nürtingen to the 'Daltons' crime group as Warsaw blames Russian intelligence

sections.text: ARD's capital studio and STRG_F reported that the two Turkish citizens arrested by Baden-Württemberg special forces in Nürtingen on a Polish European arrest warrant, Müslüm T., 34, and Ümit E., 38, belong to Turkish organised-crime circles known as the 'Daltons' [18]. Poland's special-services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said there was no doubt Russian intelligence services were behind the 23 September fire at the Wola Krobowska ground station; tagesschau noted it is unclear what evidence supports that [18]. Turkish Minute, citing Der Spiegel, reported that the pair may belong to the gang or have acted on instructions from people connected to it, and that Polish prosecutors accuse them of sabotage and of working for a foreign intelligence service [19]. Poland's ABW said on 16 October that the fire was arson, that a third person recruited over Telegram reconnoitred the site, and that it is still seeking the organisers [20].

Confidence on the arrests and charges is high, because Polish and German authorities acted on them. Confidence on the gang link is moderate, because it rests on German investigative reporting. Confidence on Russian direction is moderate, because Polish officials assert it on record but no public charge document names a handler.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: France: riot police use batons, tear gas, and water cannon against protesters in Paris, Lyon, Strasbourg, and Marseille on a nationwide day of cost-of-living protests

sections.text: Germany's dpa, citing France's Interior Ministry, reported that police used tear gas and batons against protesters in Paris, Lyon, and Strasbourg as nationwide demonstrations against high living costs began on Saturday [1]. France 24's live file, compiled with AFP, AP, and Reuters, reported police using tear gas and batons to drive demonstrators from the streets of Paris, Marseille, and Lyon, and said footage from the CLPRESS agency showed armoured riot police chasing demonstrators through Paris and striking several people after they had been knocked to the pavement [2]. The BBC reported people throwing rocks as riot police charged in Paris, and tear gas used in Strasbourg, Bordeaux, and Lyon [3]. CNN reported that police deployed tear gas at Place de la République and charged into the crowd, with a small group aiming fireworks at police lines [4]. AFP reporters saw police fire water cannon and tear gas after hundreds of mostly masked protesters, some setting off fireworks, confronted them at several points in Paris [5]. The Paris police prefecture said at 13:28 that officers at République were being attacked by hostile individuals who had come to fight and that police do not back down before rioters, and at 15:07 that several hundred people had stayed behind after the authorised march set off to attack police and rescue services, with water cannon in use [6][7]. By 14:15 the prefecture reported 133 arrests and more than 1,000 preventive checks in Paris, and the Interior Ministry counted 140 actions involving 32,800 people outside Paris and 166 arrests nationwide at midday [8]. Authorities had projected 90,000 to 170,000 protesters nationwide [9].

Confidence that police used batons is high, because the Interior Ministry's account carried by dpa, a live file drawing on three wires, and agency footage agree, and the Paris prefecture's own posts confirm the charges and water cannon. Confidence on participation and arrest figures is moderate, because they come only from the Interior Ministry and the police prefecture and were midday counts.

items.title: France: protesters briefly break into Marseille's city hall, damage a police station, and set Lyon's tourist office on fire; the CNews and Europe 1 offices are attacked in Paris

sections.text: AFP reported that masked protesters rammed the door of Marseille's city hall with security barriers and that several got in and spray-painted an anarchist symbol before police dispersed them; an AFP photographer saw protesters attack a police building in the city [5]. Marseille's police prefecture said a municipal police station in the 3rd arrondissement had windows broken and smoke bombs thrown inside [10], with no injuries reported there [8]. Mayor Benoît Payan said the intruders caused some damage and that he had to call the President, the Prime Minister, and the Interior Minister before CRS riot-police reinforcements rose from one company to five [8]. In Paris, the police prefecture said about a hundred masked people blockaded the building that houses CNews and Europe 1 early on Saturday and broke several windows, and that 21 people were detained [2][9]. BFM TV reported that masked people smashed the windows of Lyon's tourist office on Place Bellecour before it caught fire and was looted, and Reuters carried the report [9][11]. The Rhône prefecture said police were manoeuvring to disperse violent groups while firefighters were kept from reaching the fire, and in Rennes the Brittany prefecture reported burning barricades on the ring road [10].

Confidence on the Marseille city hall intrusion and the CNews blockade is high, because AFP witnessed the first and prefectures and several outlets confirm both. Confidence on the Lyon fire is moderate, because it rests on one broadcaster's report carried by a wire and a live file, with no official damage assessment yet.

items.title: France: the Interior Ministry blames the 'ultra-left' and orders 'great firmness' as the month-old school protest movement reaches 7,950 people held in custody and 937 police and gendarmes injured

sections.text: On Friday President Emmanuel Macron said the right to protest comes with respect for people and property and called the presence of people seeking only to cause damage unacceptable [12]. On Saturday people around Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told BFM TV that the day showed a very strong mobilisation of the ultra-left seeking only to create disorder, cited attempted looting, attacks on police, and the targeting of seats of power and the media, and said the minister had reminded prefects and police of his instructions for great firmness [13]. Reuters reported that Nuñez said stun grenades, suspended for the school protests after a 15-year-old lost a hand, could be used on Saturday, and that the police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence [14]. Interior Ministry figures reported by CNews put the toll since the school protests began in mid-September at 7,950 people held in custody, 6,773 of them minors, 937 police and gendarmes, 248 pupils, and 149 education staff injured, and 36 inquiries opened by the IGPN police inspectorate [15]. CNN, citing BFM TV, reported an Interior Ministry crisis meeting set for 18:00 with the chiefs of staff of the Prime Minister and the Interior and Justice Ministers [4]. Ecologist leader Marine Tondelier called the use of force completely disproportionate [8], while National Rally president Jordan Bardella blamed professionals of chaos and Jean-Luc Mélenchon's far left [9]. No injury tally for Saturday itself had been published by the cutoff.

Confidence on the government's statements is high, because they are on record and carried consistently by several outlets. Confidence on the cumulative figures is high, because they are official tallies, though they predate Saturday's protests.

items.title: French Assembly rejects the Zucman tax and a return of the wealth tax as Lecornu's 2027 budget debate runs behind schedule

sections.text: The National Assembly on Friday rejected several left-wing amendments to the 2027 finance bill that would have imposed a minimum tax of at least 2 percent of net wealth on about 1,800 of the richest households, on the Zucman model, and rejected proposals to restore the wealth tax (ISF) [16]. The government and general rapporteur Philippe Juvin (LR) opposed the measures, Juvin citing a risk of unconstitutionality and harm to business activity [16][17]. About 3,000 amendments to the revenue part remained in the early evening, with its vote scheduled for Tuesday, and the text must in principle go to the Senate by 17 November [16]. Earlier on Friday the social affairs committee rejected the 2027 social-security budget, and AFP reported Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu could in the end use Article 49.3 on both texts [18].
Confidence on the votes is high, because a national wire reported them on the day and several outlets carried it without dispute.

items.title: Fico says Slovakia and Hungary will not join a €70bn package for Ukraine; Zelensky says no EU leader backs easing Russia sanctions

sections.text: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said on 16 October that Slovakia would not take part in the €70 billion support package Zelensky requested at the Brussels summit and that Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar took a similar position, according to the Slovak agency TASR as reported by the Kyiv Independent; Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš also signalled Czechia would stay out [19]. On Saturday Zelensky said European partners were unanimous that no sanctions on Russia should be lifted until Putin stops the killing and that nobody supports the US–Russia diesel deal [20]. He said a US proposal to unfreeze part of Russia's frozen assets had been discussed with Belgium and EU leaders and was fully under Europe's control, and that no European leader had said no to the €70 billion request [20].

Confidence on Fico's position is moderate, because it reaches us through one agency relay and Magyar's stance is reported only by Fico. Confidence on Zelensky's statements is high, because they are on record, but his account of what EU leaders said is Kyiv's version, not EU text.

items.title: Commission clears Italy's energy-bills decree, letting Rome cap the gas price used to set electricity prices; Brussels says it must be temporary

sections.text: Meloni told reporters after the summit that Italy had closed its negotiation with the Commission on the energy-bills decree, which lets the government act on how gas costs feed into the electricity price in order to lower bills, and welcomed ETS2 and ETS review language in the conclusions [21]. ANSA reported that the Commission said the measure must be temporary and expects Rome's intervention plan as soon as possible, that the mechanism echoes the 2022 Iberian exception, and that ETS carbon costs on firms stay untouched [22]. Il Foglio reported Meloni did not win the wider budget flexibility she sought, against Nordic and German opposition [23], while Il Messaggero quoted her as optimistic that there are margins for more flexibility within the current rules, including for energy investment [24].
Confidence is moderate, because the government and the national agency agree on the deal but the Commission's own text was not found.

items.title: UK Defence Secretary Streeting says thousands of troops will rehearse a post-ceasefire deployment to Ukraine in Poland next month, with French, German, and Polish forces

sections.text: Speaking in Washington on his first US visit in the post, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said thousands of personnel will take part next month in a major exercise in Poland to make sure the coalition of the willing is ready to support Ukraine after the war [25]. GB News reported the drill will include French, German, and Polish troops, was agreed at a coalition summit in July, and, citing The Times, will rehearse moving troops, food, and fuel into a post-conflict Ukraine [26]. The Independent set the announcement against President Trump declining to say Putin started the war [25]. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk had announced in July that the coalition's first exercises, with British and French forces, would be held in Poland in the autumn [27]; Rzeczpospolita reported on 14 October that no date had been fixed and that Polish officers it spoke to unofficially were unsure of the timing [28].
Confidence is moderate, because the announcement is on record but participating states' own confirmations were not located.

items.title: After the summit, Costa says he will accelerate budget talks for a year-end deal while von der Leyen calls the current negotiating frame a 'straitjacket'

sections.text: European Council President Antonio Costa wrote at 20:44 CEST that the EU must agree its next long-term budget by the end of the year and that he will now accelerate the work [29]. Xinhua reported von der Leyen told the closing press conference that the latest frame would cut flexibility by 50 percent against the current budget and leave 99.5 percent of funds predetermined, calling it a straitjacket [30]. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said after the summit that the Irish presidency's proposal is insufficient and well below the current budget, and that Spain will be a net contributor in the next period [31]. Von der Leyen wrote at 20:05 CEST that Europe will step up for Ukraine's additional needs and that global partners must too [32]. Euronews reported leaders condemned the US-Russia diesel deal while the Bulgarian prime minister broke ranks to support it [33].

Confidence on Costa's and von der Leyen's stated positions is high, because they come from their own posts. Confidence on the flexibility figures is low, because only one state-media source carried them.

items.title: Frederiksen asks the Commission to examine Spain's mass regularisation of migrants; Sanchez likens Babis's 'population replacement' charge to far-right rhetoric

sections.text: El Pais reported that after the 18-country migration breakfast Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she had asked the Commission to examine what happens when a country does almost the exact opposite of the rest, and that Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis spoke of politicians capable of population replacement [34]. Euronews reported that Pedro Sanchez rejected the criticism from Babis, Frederiksen, and Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker as not matching the figures, separated his disagreement with Frederiksen from Babis's remarks, which he said sound like Spain's Vox, and that Stocker called the plan a bad signal [35]. Euronews reported Babis warned Czechia could tighten border controls against migrants arriving from other EU states [35].
Confidence on what the leaders said is high, because two independent sources quote them directly and the quotes match.

items.title: Tusk vows not to yield in the Constitutional Tribunal standoff and rejects giving Nawrocki a share of ambassador nominations

sections.text: Speaking to reporters after the Brussels summit, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the key aim was to unseat Bogdan Swieczkowski, whom he called the illegally serving president of the Constitutional Tribunal, and that the government would not back down [36]. Tusk said small but aggressive groups were gathering outside the Tribunal, that coaches of PiS supporters and others were expected on Saturday, and that police would act firmly against clear aggression; Wirtualna Polska reported that a police officer was attacked near the Tribunal on Friday [36]. Tusk said he would not accept terms giving President Karol Nawrocki a share of ambassador posts, that nominations require the foreign minister's proposal, his consent, and the president's signature, and that the president may refuse a specific candidate if he gives reasons [37].
Confidence on what Tusk said is high, because two outlets quote the same briefing consistently.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Tallinn opens its first public street shelter, a Ukrainian-tested module, and plans 40 to 50 more

sections.text: Tallinn's city government showed its first public street shelter on Juhkentali Street, a module for about 20 people donated by the security firm Citysec that protects against blast and fragments from an explosion 50 metres away but not a direct missile hit [1]. Deputy mayor Tiit Terik said the door stays shut in peacetime and opens remotely in an emergency, or automatically if power and communications fail [1]. A municipal police civil-protection specialist said the module was built half by Ukrainian and half by Estonian partners and has been used in Ukraine for years [1]. ERR's Russian service reported a shelter can cost up to EUR 70,000 and that the city plans a framework tender for 40 to 50 modules next year, with sites still to be chosen [2].
Confidence is moderate, because the opening is documented by two ERR services with named officials, but the tender plan rests on officials' statements alone.

items.title: Estonia and Latvia at odds over a EUR 200 million wind-and-battery park on the border feeding the third interconnector

sections.text: ERR reported that the Lode hybrid park, 18 wind turbines with four-hour battery storage that Utilitas Wind is building in Latvia, has become a point of contention because its impact falls mostly on Estonian villages; Mulgi rural municipality challenged the project in a Latvian court without success [3]. Utilitas chief executive Priit Koit said the park connects to the third Estonia–Latvia interconnector and will feed power to either side depending on demand; groundworks and first foundations are under way near Arakste, first power is expected in about a year and completion in the first half of the year after next [3]. Einars Cilinskis, parliamentary secretary of Latvia's climate and energy ministry, said up to EUR 300,000 a year will go to the municipality and local residents [3].
Confidence is low, because the account rests on one broadcaster's report and neither government's formal position was located.

items.title: Lukashenko, near the Latvian border, says Minsk does not want war with NATO and accuses the Baltic states of 'insolent' behaviour

sections.text: RIA Novosti reported that Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko, visiting a people's militia unit in Verkhnedvinsk district of Vitebsk region near the Latvian border, said Minsk does not want war with NATO, accused the neighbouring Baltic states of insolent behaviour that provokes larger Western states, and said weapons including drones had been prepared for militia units [4]. On 13 October, before this window, BelTA quoted him saying the reported incursion of an armed group from Belarus was "entirely staged by the Latvians themselves as a media stunt to get money from the European Union" [5]. LRT had reported that masked people smugglers bringing 20 migrants to the border pelted Latvian soldiers with stones and one drew an object resembling a pistol [6].
Confidence on what Lukashenko said is moderate, because one Russian state agency carried the remarks, though they repeat a line he used four days earlier.

items.title: Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, and Poland jointly ask Costa and von der Leyen to fund Rail Baltica's completion in the 2028–2034 EU budget, citing military mobility

sections.text: President Gitanas Nausėda said in Brussels that all four states building Rail Baltica had written to European Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen asking that funds in the next financial framework let them finish the project, and said its importance is both economic and military [7]. The presidency said the leaders committed to completing the line within the 2028–2034 budget period and stressed that the current security environment has raised its value for moving EU and NATO troops and equipment quickly [7]. Nausėda acknowledged that the project had been delayed for objective and subjective reasons [7].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on the Lithuanian presidency's statement relayed by the public broadcaster; the letter itself was not read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Albania: on the fifth day of protests, police fire stun grenades, tear gas, and water cannon outside the Education Ministry; police count 500 detained and 165 injured

sections.text: AFP reported that police used tear gas and water cannon while protesters threw stones and burned rubbish bins to block roads, that fighting continued into the night in several parts of Tirana, and that protesters tried to force their way into government offices on the main boulevard on Friday [1]. Interior Minister Ervin Demo said 156 people had been injured in recent days, 97 of them police, called the unrest a disguised attempt to seize power through violence, and said two officers had been suspended after two cases of excessive force [1]. In a video address Prime Minister Edi Rama said it was not a student phenomenon and blamed foreign hands; protests also hit Elbasan, Shkodra, and Korca [2]. Police said 160 people were detained for violence on Thursday evening [2]. Earlier on Friday DW cited police figures of 71 officers injured [3]. On Saturday, the fifth day of the student-led movement, Reuters reported that thousands gathered outside the Education Ministry in Tirana and that, after masked youths threw rocks at riot police, officers answered with stun grenades, tear gas, and a water cannon; police figures showed 500 protesters detained, 330 of them released, and 120 police and 45 protesters registered as injured, and noted that many injuries to protesters may have gone unrecorded [4]. Panorama reported renewed stone-throwing and tear gas outside the ministry later in the day [5].

Confidence on the clashes is high, because a wire and local outlets report them independently. Confidence on the casualty and detention figures is moderate, because they come only from the police and the government.

items.title: Serbia: Vučić holds his first Novi Sad rally since the station collapse, with Slovakia's Fico on stage; two journalists assaulted beforehand

sections.text: N1 reported that Vučić, lead candidate of United Serbia, spoke in front of the Serbian National Theatre in Novi Sad for the first time since the railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, to a crowd bussed in from elsewhere, with police closing much of the centre [6]. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico addressed the rally, praised Vučić, and said Slovakia would keep respecting Serbia's territorial integrity, including on Kosovo; Vučić accused unnamed foreign powers of financing protests and promised justice for the victims [6]. Danas reported the rally began at 18:00 and that Vučić asked the crowd to greet Milorad Dodik and said those responsible for the collapse must answer for any crime [7]. Vučić posted three rally messages on X between 20:38 and 22:35 calling for a united Serbia [8]. N1 said a Razglas News journalist was attacked and a Mašina reporter assaulted before the event [6]. N1's Bosnian service reported that flags bearing the image of Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb commander serving a life sentence for genocide at Srebrenica, flew above the crowd next to the list's banners [9].
Confidence is moderate, because the rally and the speakers are corroborated by two outlets and the candidate's own posts, but the assault claims come from one outlet.

items.title: Serbia: Student List marchers set off from Zaječar for the 22 October Slavija rally as SNS stages a counter-event in Aleksinac

sections.text: N1 reported that students and supporters left Zaječar on a six-day walk to Belgrade via Bor, Žagubica, Petrovac na Mlavi, Požarevac, and Smederevo for the Student List rally at Slavija Square on 22 October; about 70 people had registered [10]. In Aleksinac, SNS activists set up unannounced stands across the street from a Student List gathering announced two days earlier, and N1's reporter counted at least 15 buses arriving, many apparently from Niš [11].
Confidence is low, because both reports come from a single outlet without independent corroboration.

items.title: Serbia: N1 says ten of its journalists have left the channel nine days before the election

sections.text: The N1 newsroom said ten colleagues, among them Žaklina Tatalović, Danica Vučenić, and Mia Bjelogrlić, had decided to leave, calling the timing particularly worrying and saying that for months it had had to adapt to colleagues using every legal basis to take leave [12]. The statement said the newsroom would assess whether to replace them and would keep its professional principles [12].
Confidence is low, because the only account is the channel's own statement and the cause of the departures is not documented.

items.title: Montenegro: after Croatia has the year-end deadline cut from EU summit conclusions, Plenković and Janša say the open issues can be settled

sections.text: Croatian public broadcaster HRT reported on Friday morning that, at Prime Minister Andrej Plenković's request, the European Council's conclusions on Montenegro dropped draft wording calling for agreement on provisionally closing all negotiating chapters by the end of this year and for finishing the accession treaty as soon as possible; Plenković set out eight Croatian demands that Montenegro should meet before Zagreb agrees to close the talks [13]. At the close of the summit Plenković said, as reported by Serbian broadcaster RTS, that Croatia had changed the conclusions on its own initiative to send Podgorica a realistic message to focus on talks with Zagreb, and that the few open issues were solvable [14]. Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Janša said after the summit that Slovenia supports Montenegro's membership, that the open issues with Croatia are more symbolic than difficult and could be resolved in the coming months, and that several talks on them would be held soon [15].

Confidence is moderate, because the change to the conclusions is reported consistently by Croatian outlets and acknowledged by Plenković himself, but the in-window statements come through relayed reports and the final text was not read at source.

items.title: Croatia: police arrest Hajduk Split fans over pro-Nazi and antisemitic chants before the Ajax match; the government condemns them

sections.text: BIRN reported that police in Split arrested several members of the Torcida fan group after a march with chants including "Auschwitz, Auschwitz" and "Rise, Adolf" before Thursday's match against Ajax; the case is being investigated as hate speech, further arrests were expected on Friday, and the Croatian government, Split's mayor, and political parties condemned it [16]. BBC Sport reported the police investigation and that ombudswoman Tena Simonović Einwalter condemned the incident [17].
Confidence on the arrests and the condemnations is high, because two independent outlets report them; the investigating judge's decision was not yet public.

items.title: BIRN: Serbia's foreign ministry gave at least €250,000 since 2023 to diaspora groups aligned with the ruling SNS

sections.text: A BIRN investigation published by Balkan Insight found that the Serbian Foreign Ministry's Directorate for the Diaspora gave at least €250,000 since 2023 to diaspora associations in North Macedonia, Bosnia, and Serbia that campaign for President Vučić's SNS. The ministry did not respond to BIRN's questions [18].
Confidence is moderate, because the records are documentary but no other outlet or official has yet tested them.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the South Caucasus

items.title: Iran's Pezeshkian says he and Pashinyan discussed a joint Armenia–Iran strategic document; experts to hold follow-up meetings

sections.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that in his Yerevan meeting with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan the two reviewed relations and discussed preparing a joint strategic document, and that experts had agreed to hold specialised meetings to lay the groundwork [1]. Earlier on 16 Oct, Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan said the strategic cooperation document with Iran was practically agreed and would be signed at the next convenient opportunity, adding that a Pashinyan visit to Iran was planned but undated [2]. Iranian agency Tasnim's account of the meeting has Pezeshkian calling for a long-term strategic plan and Pashinyan citing energy and trade potential [3].
Moderate confidence in the reporting, based on matching Iranian and Armenian official statements; low confidence in timing, because both sides gave no date.

items.title: Georgia: Kobakhidze meets Iran's Pezeshkian in Yerevan as Tehran calls for 'practical cooperation' and criticises US sanctions

sections.text: Civil.ge reported that Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on 16 October on the sidelines of the COP17 biodiversity conference in Yerevan, where they discussed bilateral relations and the Middle East [4]. Kobakhidze wrote that Georgia firmly supports diplomatic efforts toward peaceful resolution of conflicts in the region, the government press service highlighted cooperation in tourism, and Pezeshkian called for practical cooperation in the economy and tourism while criticising US sanctions on Iran [4].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one outlet citing both governments' readouts.

items.title: Georgia: Ivanishvili makes a rare public appearance to chair Georgian Dream meetings as the party faces prosecutions of former officials and a party-ban case

sections.text: Bidzina Ivanishvili, the US-sanctioned founder and honorary chair of Georgian Dream, chaired meetings of the party's political council and parliamentary majority on 17 October, and Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said afterwards that they focused on domestic and foreign policy issues without giving details [5]. Civil.ge set the appearance against resignations, prosecutions, and arrests involving former senior officials, including former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, and the Constitutional Court's upcoming consideration of a lawsuit to ban several opposition parties [5].
Confidence on the meetings is moderate, because one outlet reports them with the Prime Minister's on-record comment, and their content was not disclosed.

items.title: Georgia: shares in the UK-sanctioned pro-government Imedi TV's owner are redistributed to four insiders

sections.text: Registry documents filed on 16 October show that Georgian Media Production Group, owner of the British-sanctioned pro-government channel Imedi, is now held in equal 25 percent shares by four people: general director Mariam Lomidze, presenter Irakli Chikhladze, programming head Maia Chigoshvili, and new shareholder Magda Anikashvili, a host and supervisory-board member [6]. Prime Media Global, owned by businessman Ilia Mikelaishvili, which held 50 percent, and two other executives no longer hold shares [6].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one outlet's reading of public registry documents.

items.title: Azerbaijan: parliament blames 'hostile forces' in 'friendly and neighbouring countries' for hybrid attacks as school protests over a hijab ban enter a second week

sections.text: Azerbaijan's parliament said the country faces intensified hybrid attacks from hostile forces operating from the territory of friendly and neighbouring countries, carried out in the digital space by hacker groups, foreign media, real and fake accounts, and bots; OC Media noted the statement followed a 14 October cyber-attack on state internet services, claimed by a pro-Iranian group citing the school hijab restrictions, which Baku said affected 100 domains [7]. DW reported nearly a week of unprecedented protests by schoolchildren against the headscarf ban, disrupted access to Instagram and TikTok as videos spread, and an unusual exchange of criticism between Azerbaijani and Turkish politicians [8].
Confidence on the statement and the protests is moderate, because two independent outlets report them, but the cyber-attack attribution rests on the hackers' own claim.

items.title: Azerbaijan–Turkey rift: Baku declares a Turkish columnist wanted over alleged coup calls, and Ankara bristles after Israel's Herzog flies in on an Azerbaijani airliner

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Prosecutor General's Office said on 16 October it had opened a criminal case over social-media posts allegedly promoting religious radicalism, a coup, and the forcible change of the constitutional order, charging Turkish columnist Celal Çiftçi of Şanlıurfa Olay and declaring him internationally wanted; OC Media later added that Çiftçi had publicly apologised [9]. OC Media also reported outrage in Ankara after Israeli President Isaac Herzog bypassed a Turkish ban on using its airspace by flying to Baku on a commercial Azerbaijan Airlines jet, with Turkish officials saying they were unaware he was aboard and the pro-government Azerbaijani outlet APA criticising the Turkish uproar [10].

Confidence on the criminal case is moderate, because it rests on the prosecutor's statement as reported by one outlet. Confidence on the Herzog flight row is moderate, because one outlet reports both sides' reactions.

items.title: Georgia: October 4 defendant Giorgi Kirvalidze detained on new contempt-of-court charges as he left detention

sections.text: Civil.ge reported that Giorgi Kirvalidze, an athlete charged over the 4 October 2025 election-day unrest, was detained on 16 October on criminal charges of insulting a judge as he left a seven-day administrative sentence for swearing at Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili. Officers cited Article 366(2) of the Criminal Code, which carries up to two years in prison [11]. Interpressnews carried activist Tamuna Giorgadze's account that he was detained outside the Gurjaani facility [12].
Confidence is moderate, because the detention is documented by two outlets but no official charge text has been published.

theaters.heading: Politics, the Bundeswehr, the economy, and developments in Baden-Württemberg

items.title: Merz tells the Junge Union 'there are limits for me too' on the coalition and promises a strict pension reform after Winkel's re-election

sections.text: Johannes Winkel was re-elected chairman of the Junge Union at its Deutschlandtag in Bonn with 265 votes, his best result [1], and before the congress said a collapse of the planned pension reform would be a failure the federal government could hardly recover from [2]. Addressing about 300 delegates on Saturday, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he wants the coalition to succeed but does not put its survival above every policy outcome it must deliver: 'There are limits for me too' [3]. He said the pension package should reach cabinet this year with a first reading before the turn of the year, that penalty-free retirement after 45 years should go, and that the pension commission's proposals should come unchanged; one delegate called on him to resign [4]. Merz said the CDU would stand no chance at the next election unless it showed sustained growth and reformed social systems [5][6], said anyone in the party who backs electing AfD members to state office has no place in the CDU, and warned SPD and Greens against talks with the Left in Berlin [3].
Confidence is high, because public broadcasters and the Stuttgarter Zeitung report the speech consistently and quote it directly.

items.title: New Labour Minister Schweitzer seeks a ‘good compromise’ on keeping penalty-free retirement after 45 years of contributions

sections.text: Alexander Schweitzer (SPD), sworn in as federal labour minister on Wednesday, told the Rheinpfalz he wants a good compromise in the coalition dispute over penalty-free retirement after 45 contribution years, and said further political debate on it was needed [7]. The government's pension commission proposed abolishing the rule in June, Schweitzer opposed abolition in August, and he noted the coalition agreement keeps it in principle [7]. Handelsblatt's overnight federal-politics file carries the same interview line [8].
Moderate confidence, based on the public broadcaster's relay of a named interview and the open coalition dispute.

items.title: Berlin: Left, Greens, and SPD conclude exploratory talks and, according to dpa and AFP, agree to open coalition negotiations

sections.text: tagesschau reported that the Left, Greens, and SPD concluded exploratory talks four weeks after the Berlin election and would give a joint statement at 17:00; dpa and AFP, citing party sources, reported agreement to open coalition negotiations [9]. The Greens have called a small party congress for Monday and the Left a congress on 31 October, so negotiations could begin in early November [9]. Chancellor Merz told the Junge Union the same day that anyone who wants to strengthen the political centre must not hold talks with left radicals [3].
Confidence is moderate, because the agreement rests on party sources relayed by two agencies ahead of the parties' own statement.

items.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD, Left, and Greens report first coalition results — state job cuts, digitalisation, and a Land development bank

sections.text: Five days into coalition talks, SPD, Left, and Greens in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania drew a positive interim balance, Minister-President Manuela Schwesig (SPD) calling the talks constructive [10]. They agreed on savings in state administration, staff cuts, and digitalisation alongside targeted investment, funding for affordable housing and AI, and a Land development bank [10]. The parties aim to finish talks in three weeks; the new Landtag meets for the first time within days [10].
Moderate confidence, based on agency copy quoting the Minister-President and a stated three-week timetable.

items.title: Merz and Macron agree to loosen the EU's 2035 combustion-engine phase-out in exchange for 'Made in Europe' rules; Baden-Württemberg's car sector welcomes it

sections.text: In a joint statement France and Germany proposed a package combining "an ambitious European decarbonisation pathway with the regulatory flexibility needed" and incentives for European production [11]. tagesschau reported that the deal would let cars with combustion engines be newly registered in the EU after 2035 and could give the Council a majority for the Commission's December proposal, which the European Parliament must also approve [12]. Euronews reported that the package requires a 90% CO2 cut rather than 100% and links support to European-content rules, and quoted Merz saying the phaseout of combustion engines "is now off the table" [13]. Merz wrote at 11:49 CEST that it was a good day for drivers and for jobs in Germany, France, and Europe [14]; DW carried his and Macron's remarks [15]. Stuttgarter Zeitung reported broadly positive reactions in Baden-Württemberg [16]. Later on Friday Merz said in Brussels that the combustion-engine phase-out was now history, and Environment Minister Carsten Schneider (SPD) backed the agreement, saying it gives carmakers more room on CO2 limits so they can invest in electric mobility and European sites [17].

Confidence on the Franco-German position is high, because the joint statement is published and both governments' ministers spoke on record. How other member states will vote was not public by the cutoff.

items.title: Union parliamentary leader Frei demands changes to Klingbeil's sugar-tax bill, including transition periods for drinks makers

sections.text: CDU/CSU parliamentary group leader Thorsten Frei told the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger that Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil's draft law for the planned tax on sugared drinks needs changes, calling for transition periods so manufacturers can change their recipes and saying the tax must create no new administrative posts [18]. He defended the tax in principle but warned that makers unable to reformulate would have to raise prices, risking competitive disadvantages and job losses [19]. The federal cabinet approved a proposal on Wednesday for the coalition groups to bring into the Bundestag, and CSU group leader Alexander Hoffmann has already called for a start in early 2028 instead of July 2027 [18]. Tagesspiegel carries the same agency report [20].
Moderate confidence, based on agency copy quoting a named interview and the CSU's earlier stated demand for a later start.
